study type: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional surveys (WHO Global Survey and Multi-country Survey)
cohort: Women with singleton neonates delivered between 22 and <37 weeks of gestation (15,471 from 21 countries in the Global Survey and 15,053 from 21 countries in the Multi-country Survey).
finding: Compared to vaginal birth, Cesarean section was associated with significantly increased odds of maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal near miss, and neonatal intensive care unit admission but significantly decreased odds of fresh stillbirth and perinatal death.
mod_finding: Compared to vaginal birth, Cesarean section was associated with significantly increased odds of maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal near miss, and neonatal intensive care unit admission but significantly decreased odds of fresh stillbirth and perinatal death.
